Statement admits m=0; Definition of the Euclidean inner product explicitly includes R^0. Proof 1.1 divides epsilon by m, and 3.1 divides by sqrt(m). For U=R^0 and any f, the only linear map from R^0 has identically zero increment remainder; a separate vacuous epsilon-delta case closes the proof. This is a missing boundary case, not a false conclusion. All positive-domain steps check by coordinate telescoping and vector MVT; if output dimension is zero it is likewise immediate. Owned lemma uses m=d+1>=2 and the Euler state-fiber application has d>=1, so neither uses the gap. Current published raw SHA256 51f5c145f2c831786179aef798b8cc387dba82a83072e2ec3d376ca32286c45b, wrapped as {item_sha256:raw} and canonically hashed, exactly reproduces routed observed_sha256 2a0dddae65057a657a382170469039bb4b93c5c261b4be2891471ee509870378. Under the local solution definition the domain need only contain a neighborhood of the initial time, so the union family need not consist solely of open intervals. At each t in a family member J, local existence gives z near (t,x(t)); uniqueness on J intersect dom(z) makes it agree with x. Their union extends the original solution, is still local through t0, and contains a neighborhood of t, proving I open. The cited overlap/gluing lemma supplies exactly this immediate argument. The union is a solution locally by those extensions, all solutions agree on overlap, and every solution through the data is contained in the union since it extends locally around t0. This completes the two-step argument without a missing substantial prerequisite. Nonfatal omitted inference recorded for owner polish; Euler F7/Proof 1.1 uses the sound continuous locally state-Lipschitz interface. Published carrier remains unchanged.
